description: Composite of four back-scattered electron (BSE) SEM micrographs of Zr-alloyed Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels prior to tensile deformation; grey level gives phase/crystallographic contrast. (a) Zr0, 25 µm scale bar: equiaxed polygonal grains with uniform grey variation, annotated "Coarse FCC", i.e. a homogeneous coarse-grained FCC structure with a few isolated dark particles. (b) Zr0.01, 25 µm: the same coarse FCC grain structure plus one region of distinctly finer grains outlined by a cyan dashed line and labelled "Fine FCC". (c) Zr0.50, 50 µm: a clearly banded heterogeneous structure in which cyan-dashed "Fine FCC" bands alternate with large "Coarse FCC" regions; a red rectangle labelled "c1" marks the area magnified in the next panel. (c1) 10 µm: enlargement of that fine-grained band, showing a dense, uniform dispersion of fine FCC grains and particles. The group therefore demonstrates that raising Zr from 0 to 0.50 wt.% converts a homogeneous coarse-grained FCC microstructure into a bimodal coarse + fine FCC heterogeneous grain structure; no numeric grain sizes are printed on any panel, only scale bars.

observations.observation: Panel (a) (sample Zr0) shows a single population of coarse, equiaxed polygonal grains annotated "Coarse FCC"; no fine-grained region is present.
Panel (b) (sample Zr0.01) contains coarse FCC grains plus one cyan-dashed-outlined region of markedly finer grains labelled "Fine FCC".
Panel (c) (sample Zr0.50) shows a banded heterogeneous structure: cyan-dashed "Fine FCC" bands running through large "Coarse FCC" regions.
Panel (c1) is an enlargement of the red-boxed area of (c) and shows a dense, uniform dispersion of fine FCC grains/particles.
Printed scale bars are 25 µm in (a), 25 µm in (b), 50 µm in (c) and 10 µm in (c1); no numerical grain-size values are printed anywhere in the figure.
Small dark-contrast particles (brighter/darker than the FCC matrix) are visible in all four panels, most distinctly as isolated dark dots within the FCC grains.
The caption identifies the imaged material as Zr-alloyed Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steels prior to deformation, with panels assigned to Zr0 (a), Zr0.01 (b) and Zr0.50 (c, c1).
The citing text states that the Zr-free steel consists mainly of coarse recrystallized FCC grains, indicating full recrystallization after annealing at 900 °C.
The citing text states that the Zr0.01 steel consists of coarse FCC grains and few fine FCC grains.
The citing text describes the Zr0.50 steel as a typical heterogeneous structure of coarse FCC (CG) and fine FCC (FG) grains, as captured in Fig. 1c.
The citing text states that the enlarged BSE image (Fig. 1c1) clearly reveals a high density of fine FCC particles uniformly distributed in the FG regions.

Grain sizes can only be compared qualitatively through the scale bars: coarse grains appear of order tens of micrometres in (a)-(c), whereas (c1) resolves grains roughly an order of magnitude smaller.

subfigures.description: BSE-SEM micrograph of the Zr0 steel with a 25 µm scale bar; only coarse equiaxed polygonal FCC grains (blue label "Coarse FCC") and a few small dark particles.
BSE-SEM micrograph of the Zr0.01 steel with a 25 µm scale bar; predominantly coarse FCC grains (labelled "Coarse FCC") with one cyan-dashed-outlined patch of much finer grains labelled "Fine FCC".

BSE-SEM micrograph of the Zr0.50 steel with a 50 µm scale bar; heterogeneous banded structure with cyan-dashed "Fine FCC" bands interleaved with large "Coarse FCC" regions; a red rectangle labelled "c1" marks the magnified area.

Higher-magnification BSE-SEM micrograph (10 µm scale bar) of the red-boxed region of (c), labelled "Fine FCC"; shows a dense, uniformly distributed population of fine FCC grains/particles plus dark-contrast second-phase particles.
